name: Agents Platform Runners
description: Depends on the code-agent-clis app (claude/codex/copilot/cursor-agent already installed at /usr/local/bin, single source of truth) so this workspace's agent-CLI runners are what agents-platform-multitenant's agent sessions use, and contributes the ported "aw-agents" MCP (agent_mcp.py) so agents-platform is controllable as MCP tools from this workspace.

skills.description: How to reply to messages routed through a Telegram bot connected to this workspace via agents-platform — markers for attachments/buttons/mini-apps/location, voice vs text, tone, and delivery contract for a CLI agent session spawned by this app's runner. Ported and adapted from the agentic-workspace monolith's WorkspaceAgent skill of the same name.

The Supervisor tool — 3 MCP tools (supervise/stop_supervisor/supervisor_status) any Agents Platform agent can call to watch another session's whole run chain and get woken up exactly once when it goes idle.

Generic coding-specialist contract for the "Coder" Agents Platform agent — orients it to what Agents Platform is, makes a knowledge-base search mandatory before starting any task, and sets baseline engineering conduct.

Code-review contract for the "Code Reviewer" Agents Platform agent — reads a diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification cleanups, verifies each finding against the code before reporting it, and never fixes what it reviews. Distinct from aw-agent-qa: QA judges whether a delivery matches its request, this one judges the code itself.

Generic root-cause-analysis contract for the "Debugger" Agents Platform agent — debugs by explicit hypothesis and small experiments, reports the root cause with its evidence, and hands the fix to a Coder rather than writing it. Points at the aw-debugger DAP tools while stating up front that no DAP server ships with them.
Generic documentation-writer contract for the "Doc Writer" Agents Platform agent — writes README/ADR/module/API docs grounded in the actual code.
Generic QA-review contract for the "QA" Agents Platform agents — validates a finished task's delivery and decides the outcome (Kanban status if a card system is wired up, otherwise a plain verdict).
Contract for the "UX Coder" Agents Platform agent — owns end-to-end delivery of a UX-Proto prototype, with a strong mandate for usability.

Guided agent/workflow execution via the agent-mcp server — the conductor is a MANAGER who delegates to platform agents through discovery → exploration → decomposition → plan approval → execution → validation → iteration → final report, never executing the work itself.

The Agents Flow handoff contract — the three terminal actions (run_agent_async / return_to_caller_agent / mark_flow_done) an agent must end its turn with when it is a node in an enabled flow. agents-platform's executor auto-injects this skill at dispatch, so it must exist in the workspace skills tree or every flow agent runs without the contract and gets escalated to a human.

agents_platform_base.description: Base URL of the agents-platform-multitenant instance this app's MCP tools control. 172.18.0.1 is the agentic-workspace_default bridge gateway (== the real host) — the only address reachable from aw-app-mcp-gateway's nested podman namespace; override if your workspace's network subnet differs.

agents_platform_token.description: aw-backend identity JWT sent as Authorization: Bearer on every call to agents_platform_base — required, agents-platform-multitenant's require_identity() rejects unauthenticated requests with 401. Mint one inside the aw-backend container: python -c "from src.api.identity_auth import create_identity_jwt; print(create_identity_jwt(<user_id>, [{'workspace': 'aw', 'role': 'owner'}], expiry_seconds=<seconds>))"

execute_secret.description: Shared secret RunnerLLM (agents-platform-multitenant) must present as the X-Runner-Secret header on every POST /execute call. This app is registered PUBLIC in aw-backend's AppInstall registry (bypasses the tunnel edge's aw_id_jwt+membership check), so this secret — combined with aw-workspace's own per-app IdentityGuard, which still requires a validly-signed identity JWT — is the real access control for /execute. Generate with e.g. `python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))"` and configure the SAME value on agents-platform-multitenant's Runner row / RunnerLLM env.

own_base_url.description: Override for this app's own reachable base URL, sent to agents-platform-multitenant on POST /register as the Runner row's base_url. Defaults to https://agents-platform-runners.app.<workspace>.workspace.aw.tekflox.com (the per-app subdomain shape, bare host/path — verified-reachable via the same public BYOD tunnel edge) — only override if this workspace's public domain differs.

shared_redis_url.description: OPTIONAL since 0.26.0 — leave blank and it is derived automatically. Full redis:// URL (with password + db index) of the SAME shared Redis instance agents-platform-multitenant uses for its Redis-Stream run-event transport (its AP_REDIS_URL). /execute publishes each spawned CLI agent's stdout lines to run:{run_id}:events on this Redis so RunnerLLM can attach and replay exactly like a local docker-CLI run. Verified 2026-08-02: reachable from this workspace via the docker bridge gateway IP, e.g. redis://:<password>@172.18.0.1:6379/1 — aw-sandbox's own DNS name does NOT resolve from inside this workspace's nested podman netns, only the numeric gateway IP does. When blank, agents_platform_runners_app/shared_redis.py falls back to AW_SHARED_REDIS_URL, then to redis://<this container's default-route gateway>:6379/1 (db 1 = the db agents-platform-multitenant attaches its consumer groups on; override with AW_SHARED_REDIS_DB). Set this only when the shared Redis is NOT on the bridge gateway or needs a password — a freshly created workspace must not require pasting it by hand.

kanban_sweep_enabled.title: Kanban Ready sweep
kanban_sweep_enabled.description: Poll the Notion Kanban board every kanban_sweep_interval_s and dispatch every card sitting in Ready — the trigger that replaces the monolith's POST /api/notion/webhook, so a card moved to Ready produces a run in THIS agents-platform rather than the legacy one. OFF by default on purpose: the monolith's webhook is still registered and live, and this flag is the entire cut-over (tick it) and the entire rollback (untick it), with no deploy on either side. Running both at once is safe by design — each side leases the card by writing a unique token into AgentRunId and reading it straight back (kanban_dispatch.claim_card), so exactly one can win, and a failed read makes both stand down and leave the card in Ready for the next tick. Takes effect on the next tick — no app restart needed either way.

kanban_sweep_interval_s.title: Kanban sweep interval (s)
kanban_sweep_interval_s.description: Seconds between Ready-card sweeps. Latency is 0 to this, averaging half. 60s is the default because the webhook it replaces was measured at ~50s on a real card and its own code cites up to ~3min worst case — so 60s is at worst a wash. Lower costs Notion API calls against a ~3 req/s pace; 30s is safe if latency starts to matter.

public.title: Public
public.description: Expose this app through the workspace's public tunnel routing layer (aw-backend's own AppInstall.config.public flag, same mechanism mcp-gateway's own "Public" setting uses) — required for POST /execute to be reachable at all: agents-platform-multitenant's RunnerLLM calls this app's own_base_url over the public BYOD tunnel edge, which 401s any non-public app before the request even reaches this app's own execute_secret check. Defaulting this to true (declared in schema, not just set by hand) makes it survive an uninstall+reinstall from scratch: every config save round-trips the FULL config dict through aw-backend's AppInstall.config — a field that exists only as a manually-poked cloud-side value (not part of any app's own persisted config) gets silently dropped on the very next save. Found live 2026-08-11/12: exactly that happened after an uninstall+reinstall, and /execute kept 401ing at the tunnel edge even after the app's own execute_secret was correctly restored.

warm_container.title: Warm containers
warm_container.description: Keep one long-lived "warm" claude container per session (aw-warm-<agent_id>-<session_id>, 6h TTL) and dispatch each turn into it, instead of spawning a fresh container per turn. Turn 1 of a session is always cold — the warm container is keyed by the session_id that turn 1 produces — so reuse starts from turn 2. ON by default since 0.32.0; untick to force the per-turn ephemeral path. This lives in app config, NOT in the RUNNER_WARM_CONTAINER env var it replaces: aw-remote-host's install.sh only forwards that var into the workspace container when the HOST process has it set, so every workspace recreate (i.e. every update/deploy) silently dropped a hand-set flag and warm mode turned itself back off — observed repeatedly, last on 2026-08-12. The env var still wins when explicitly set, as a per-host escape hatch.

gateway_mcp_url.title: Gateway MCP URL (for seeded agents)
gateway_mcp_url.description: Override for the address a SPAWNED AGENT CONTAINER uses to reach this workspace's MCP gateway. Written into the mcp_config of any AgentConfig an app contributes with `mcp_servers: ["aw-gateway"]`; the bearer token for it is read from the workspace's own .mcp.json and never travels in a manifest. Blank by default: the URL then comes straight from this workspace's own .mcp.json (http://aw-app-mcp-gateway:9200/mcp), which a spawned agent container CAN resolve — verified from inside a live agent container on 2026-08-14. Only set this if that resolution genuinely fails for your deployment (e.g. a non-default bridge subnet); a stale/wrong value here silently 401s every MCP call an agent makes, with nothing in any log to say why.

openai_api_key.title: OpenAI API key
openai_api_key.description: OpenAI API key the contributed `openai-*` models below run on. Saving this panel PUTs it onto agents-platform-multitenant's own Settings.openai_api_key row (see platform_settings.py) — the platform stores it, this is just where you type it, so the models this app seeds and the key they need are configured in one place. Leave blank to leave the platform's current value alone: a blank field means "not set here", never "clear it", so saving an unrelated field on this panel cannot wipe a key entered in the platform UI. The same key also drives the platform's OpenAI TTS/STT, which read the identical setting.

apps.reason: This app contributes mcp.json definitions the MCP Gateway discovers and merges. Softened to non-required 2026-08-03: the deployed aw-remote-host workspace runs an aw-workspace build whose capability catalog predates mcp-gateway's own 'mcp:register-gateway' permission, so a strict required-dependency install of THIS app cascades into mcp-gateway manifest validation and fails with 'unknown permission' — blocking /execute entirely, which is worse than temporarily losing the mcp.json auto-merge. Revert to required:true once the deployed aw-workspace build is upgraded past the fix already on its own master (see aw-workspace's src/apps/capabilities.py).

This app doesn't install the CLIs itself — it depends on code-agent-clis having already put claude/codex/copilot/cursor-agent on /usr/local/bin, same path aw-workspace installs already reuse: one app owns installing each runner, this app just depends on that instead of re-implementing it. Softened to non-required 2026-08-03 alongside mcp-gateway above — not itself implicated in the permission failure, but the reconciler validates ALL required deps in the same pass, so leaving this required still blocks install. The CLIs are already present on /usr/local/bin from an earlier successful bootstrap; revert to required:true once dependency installs are unblocked again.
